title: Improving the Expressiveness of K-hop Message-Passing GNNs by Injecting Contextualized Substructure Information

problem.claim: Standard GNNs have expressive power equivalent at most to the 1-WL test, motivating methods that enhance graph representation expressiveness.

gap.claim: The work identifies limitations in K-hop message-passing GNNs and addresses the need to enhance their expressive power with substructure information.

contributions.claim: The authors propose a substructure encoding function intended to increase the expressive power of any K-hop message-passing GNN.
The method injects contextualized substructure information into K-hop message-passing GNNs.
The method is claimed to be more powerful than previous K-hop GNNs and 1-WL subgraph GNNs, and no less powerful than 3-WL.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that their method is provably more powerful than previous K-hop GNNs and 1-WL subgraph GNNs, and not less powerful than 3-WL.
The authors report new state-of-the-art or comparable performance across a variety of datasets.
The authors report that code is available in a public GitHub repository.

narrative_sequence.summary: GNNs are widely used for graph representation learning but standard GNN expressiveness is bounded by the 1-WL test.
Existing efforts enhance expressiveness through K-hop message passing or subgraph information.
The work proposes substructure encoding and contextualized substructure injection for K-hop GNNs.
The method is reported to have stronger or comparable theoretical power relative to specified prior models and 3-WL.
The authors report state-of-the-art or comparable results on various datasets and provide code.

source_observation.claim: K-hop message passing aggregates information from all neighbors within K hops, while subgraph-based methods use substructure information.

interpretation.claim: Increasing receptive-field range and encoding contextualized substructures are distinct strategies for improving graph-model expressiveness.

application.claim: When extending message-passing graph models, consider adding contextualized substructure encodings alongside broader neighborhood aggregation.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish which graph tasks, datasets, or structural regimes benefit most from the method.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the exact substructure encoding function or model architecture.
The abstract does not identify the evaluated datasets, baselines, metrics, or experimental conditions.
The abstract does not provide proof details for the expressiveness claims.
The abstract does not describe computational cost, limitations, or failure cases.
